title: The 12-team / 14-week schedule generator and its NFL-aware optimizer do not exist anywhere in the repository — not a route, not a script, not a config, not a doc
claimUnderTest: Prompt section 28 specifies a full fantasy schedule generator: 12 teams, 3 named divisions, weeks 1-14, 6 matchups/week, every team exactly once per week, no fantasy byes, divisional opponents twice, non-divisional once, no back-to-back repeat opponents, Jason vs Michaela forced to week 4, optimized against real 2026 NFL weeks 1-14 (NFL head-to-head + NFL bye weeks prioritised over rivalry preferences, with 8 tier-1 rivalry owners weighted).
observed: Zero implementation in any form. A whole-tree grep over all 10,409 tracked files for generate_schedule|build_schedule|schedule_generator|scheduleGenerator|makeSchedule|round.?robin|'no back-to-back'|'divisional opponent' returns 14 files, and every one is unrelated. The 100-operation live OpenAPI census contains no schedule route (only /api/public/league/matchups and /api/public/league/matchup/{...}, which READ posted Sleeper matchups). frontend/app has no schedule directory and no nav entry. The word 'division' appears nowhere as a data structure — the three division names (The Pit / Sweet Pepper Bacon / Barbacoa) exist only as inert strings inside Sleeper's league metadata blob in config/league_intel/sleeper_league_snapshot_2026-07-26.json; no module reads them. The two nearest-sounding artifacts are NOT this feature: src/public_league/playoff_odds.py::_round_robin_schedule is a synthetic pairing fallback used only to simulate UNPOSTED weeks for playoff odds (it copies observed Sleeper pair-sets by cycle residue and honours none of the stated constraints, has no division model, no week-4 pin and no NFL input), and src/bdvm/schedule.py fetches the nflverse NFL slate purely to mark per-player bye weeks for BDVM ROS weighting. Neither is user-reachable as a scheduler.

reproduction.command: git ls-files | wc -l && git ls-files -z | xargs -0 grep -lIiE 'generate_schedule|build_schedule|schedule_generator|scheduleGenerator|makeSchedule|round.?robin|no back.to.back|divisional opponent' && ls frontend/app | grep -i sched ; .venv/bin/python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/openapi.json'));print([p for p in d['paths'] if 'sched' in p])"
reproduction.expected: a module/route that emits a 14-week, 84-game bracket honouring the constraint set
reproduction.actual: 14 unrelated grep hits (playoff-odds simulation, sharp record queue, FLEX slot round-robin, news providers); `ls frontend/app | grep -i sched` returns nothing; the OpenAPI schedule-path list is []

userImpact: The user cannot generate the league schedule at all. There is no page to visit, no script to run and no output to import into Sleeper. Every constraint in the spec — including the hard 'Jason vs Michaela must be week 4' requirement — has to be satisfied by hand. The absence is silent: nothing in the UI or docs says the feature is unbuilt, so the only way to discover it is to look for a /schedule route that 404s.

priorFinding.note: Corrected prior-index search (the index is a dict with a 'findings' key, not a bare list) returns 6 hits on schedule/division/round-robin vocabulary and NONE is a fantasy schedule generator: PRIOR-A03-F13 and PRIOR-A21-F13 are both PlayoffOddsChart / playoff-odds schedule-INFERENCE findings about the synthetic pairing fallback described in my 'observed' field, and the PRIOR-A07-* schedule hits are cron schedules. No prior audit noticed this feature does not exist.

whatWorks: Nothing of this feature. Two reusable building blocks DO exist and would shorten the build: src/bdvm/schedule.py already ingests the nflverse slate (per-season sched_{year}.csv with a games.csv fallback) and derives per-team week structures with byes marked — that is the NFL head-to-head + bye-week input the optimizer needs, already written and tested (tests/bdvm/test_schedule.py). src/api/league_registry.py + config/leagues/registry.json already resolve the 12-team league. Manager identity + display-name aliasing is already solved in config/team_assignment.json::displayNameAliases.
rootCause: Feature was never started. Not a regression, not a disconnection — there is no code to disconnect.
requiredRepair: The constraint set is exactly determined and provably satisfiable, so this is a bounded build, not research: 2*3 + 8 = 14 games per team over exactly 14 weeks means the game multiset is forced and only the week assignment is free. docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W28/schedule_feasibility_proof.py constructs a conforming 14-week bracket (all 84 games, every team exactly once per week, divisional pairs twice and non-divisional once, no back-to-back rematch, Jason-Michaela pinned to week 4) with a randomized-restart greedy in well under a second — no ILP or SAT solver is needed and none is in requirements.txt. Build order: (1) config/schedule/league_2026.json holding the three divisions, the tier-1 rivalry weight list (Jason, Colin, Eric, Ty, Michaela, Ed, Roy, Joey) and the hard pins; (2) src/schedule/generator.py producing feasible brackets; (3) src/schedule/optimizer.py scoring candidates against the 2026 NFL weeks 1-14 pulled through the EXISTING src/bdvm/schedule.py fetcher — NFL head-to-head and NFL bye weeks weighted above rivalry preference per the spec; (4) GET /api/schedule/generate plus a /schedule page and a CSV/Sleeper-importable export. Estimate L: ~400-600 LOC plus tests.
dependencies: src/bdvm/schedule.py (nflverse slate — network fetch, degrades to [] offline, so the optimizer must treat the NFL layer as optional and fall back to constraint-only generation); config/leagues/registry.json; config/team_assignment.json for the manager-name vocabulary.

title: Team Assignment genuinely computes from live rosters — all 12 managers reproduced to the point on an independent recomputation, and the page renders with zero console errors
claimUnderTest: The prompt asks whether the teamAssignment tab computes or is static: favorite-NFL-team mappings for 12 managers, QB roster match +10, starter +5, backup +2, minimum threshold ~15, max 3 displayed assignments; and whether it recalculates after roster changes, has a refresh job, and invalidates its cache.
observed: It computes, per request, from the live Sleeper roster snapshot — nothing is static except the 12 favorite declarations. build_section is invoked through _SECTION_BUILDERS['teamAssignment'] on every /api/public/league/teamAssignment call inside run_in_threadpool(_build); the snapshot underneath is SWR-cached for PUBLIC_LEAGUE_CACHE_TTL=300s and the response-bytes memo is keyed on (root_league_id, snapshot.generated_at, latest_data_etag), so a rebuilt snapshot invalidates it structurally rather than by TTL. A refresh job exists: .github/workflows/public-league-warmup.yml runs every 20 minutes and asserts the section key set is present. Weights map onto the prompt's description exactly: qbAnchor 10, skillStarter 5, skillCommittee 2 (the prompt's 'backup +2' is a depth_chart_order in (2,3) committee tier), idpStarter 2, assignmentMinPoints 15, maxTeamsPerOwner 3. The 'production/draft/IDP bonuses' the prompt describes are partly real (idpStarter fires 35 times on the live payload) and partly dead (see W28-F003); no production tier exists at all — it was deliberately removed as a double-count and the module documents why.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && SECRET=$(cat /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/e2e_secret.txt) && curl -s -c /tmp/w28.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET" -o /dev/null && curl -s -b /tmp/w28.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/teamAssignment -o docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W28/team-assignment-live.json && .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W28/recompute_team_assignment.py

inputs.exampleJasonMIN: sum over MIN-rostered players of tier points

numericProof.formula: score(owner, nflTeam) = SUM over roster players on that NFL team of [10 if QB & depth_chart_order==1] + [5 if RB/WR/TE & depth==1] + [2 if RB/WR/TE & depth in (2,3)] + [2 if IDP & depth==1]; qualify if score >= 15 or isFavorite; cap 3

userImpact: None — this half works. A user reading /league?tab=teamAssignment sees numbers that are genuinely derived from the current rosters and can expand a per-player breakdown that adds up.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A03-F17 is the only prior finding touching this subsystem and it is about dead config knobs, not about whether the section computes. Its team_assignment half is now SUPERSEDED: the six *Rank thresholds and the eliteProductionTop10 / idpElite weights it named are gone from both config/team_assignment.json and src/api/team_assignment.py, and the 'thresholds = config["thresholds"] bound and never read' line it cited at :263 no longer exists (replaced by an explanatory comment at :241-248). Verified fixed. The prior audit made no claim about the section computing; that is new here.

whatWorks: All 12 managers resolve to a favorites key (5 by direct lowercase match, 7 through displayNameAliases — 'MaKayla'->michaela, 'jstuedle'->joel, 'Kich'->kitch, 'Collin'->colin, 'ughb' handled but not needed since displayName is 'Blaine'). The page loads at :3000 through request interception with HTTP 200, 92,508 bytes, 0 console errors, 12 'Show breakdown' buttons, and expanding one renders the correct per-player point list ('Philadelphia Eagles - 17 pts / +10 QB anchor / +5 RB starter / +2 RB committee'). load_config degrades to built-in defaults on a missing/corrupt/non-dict config rather than crashing the whole public contract. Assignments sort stably by lowercased display name.
dependencies: data/public_league/snapshot.json + data/public_league/nfl_players.json (Sleeper), rebuilt by the public-league snapshot refresh.

title: The rookie draft-capital tier is structurally dead — Sleeper publishes no draft_round field on any of its 12,207 player records, so two of the six configured weights can never fire, yet the UI tells every user that rookie draft capital is part of the score
claimUnderTest: src/api/team_assignment.py's module docstring says the model 'rewards ... rookie draft capital'; _score_player's T4 adds weights.rookieRound1 (+4) / rookieRound2 (+2) via _draft_round(meta) reading meta['draft_round'] or meta['draftRound']; config/team_assignment.json ships both weights as live knobs; and the /league tab's on-page explainer tells the user that additional NFL teams are derived from 'starting QBs, primary skill-position players, rookies with high draft capital, and (if IDP is enabled) starting defenders'. The same file's own docstring argues at length that 'a declared-but-unread knob is worse than no knob: editing it looks like it does something' — and then ships two.
observed: Sleeper's /v1/players/nfl payload has no draft_round key whatsoever. Across all 12,207 player records in the unpruned data/public_league/nfl_players.json, the key 'draft_round' is present 0 times and 'draftRound' 0 times (the record vocabulary is: active, age, birth_*, college, competitions, depth_chart_order, depth_chart_position, espn_id, fantasy_data_id, fantasy_positions, first/last/full_name, gsis_id, hashtag, height, high_school, injury_*, kalshi_id, metadata, news_updated, number, oddsjam_id, opta_id, pandascore_id, player_id, player_shard, position, practice_*, roto*_id, search_*, sport, sportradar_id, stats_id, status, swish_id, team, team_abbr, team_changed_at, weight, yahoo_id, years_exp). _draft_round() therefore returns None for every player on every roster, and T4 contributes exactly 0 points to every score ever produced. The league currently rosters 102 players with years_exp == 0 — i.e. 102 genuine rookies that the tier was written for — and not one of them scores a rookie point. The live payload's contributor-reason histogram contains 13 distinct reasons and zero instances of '1st-round rookie' or '2nd-round rookie'. The snapshot is not pruned (src/public_league/sleeper_client.py::fetch_nfl_players stores the vendor dict verbatim), so this is an upstream-vocabulary gap, not a local data-loss bug.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python -c "import json,collections;pl=json.load(open('data/public_league/nfl_players.json'));k=collections.Counter(x for m in pl.values() if isinstance(m,dict) for x in m);print('records',len(pl),'draft_round',k.get('draft_round',0),'draftRound',k.get('draftRound',0))" && .venv/bin/python -c "import json,collections;a=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W28/team-assignment-live.json'))['data']['assignments'];c=collections.Counter(x['reason'] for t in a for n in t['nflTeams'] for x in n['contributors']);print(dict(c))"
reproduction.expected: if the tier were live: a nonzero count of records carrying draft_round, and '1st-round rookie'/'2nd-round rookie' appearing among the live contributor reasons
reproduction.actual: records 12208 draft_round 0 draftRound 0; live reasons = {'QB anchor':16,'IDP DB starter':13,'WR committee':13,'IDP LB starter':13,'RB committee':10,'RB starter':9,'TE starter':8,'WR starter':8,'IDP DE starter':4,'IDP DL starter':2,'TE committee':2,'IDP DT starter':2,'IDP CB starter':1} — no rookie reason at any count

numericProof.formula: rookiePointsContributed = SUM over rostered rookies of (4 if draft_round==1 else 2 if draft_round==2 else 0); with draft_round universally absent every term is 0

userImpact: Two failure modes, both live today. (1) The on-page explainer at /league?tab=teamAssignment states that 'rookies with high draft capital' contribute to the score. They do not, and never have — a manager whose roster is loaded with premium rookies gets no credit for it and will read the breakdown as evidence that the model rated those rookies at zero, when in fact the model never looked. (2) config/team_assignment.json is explicitly presented as operator-editable ('Edit favorites/aliases/weights here without redeploy'), and its own _doc block invites retuning assignmentMinPoints when 'too few NFL teams qualify' — an operator who instead raises rookieRound1 to try to lift qualification will observe absolutely no change and have no way to learn why. Because 5 of 12 managers currently return exactly one NFL team (their favorite only), that is a realistic operator action.

priorFinding.note: Same DEFECT CLASS as PRIOR-A03-F17 ('a config file presents eight tunable knobs of which six do nothing, so an operator tuning them will change JSON and see no movement'), and that finding's specific keys are confirmed FIXED. But the fix was incomplete and the prior audit missed why: it identified the inert knobs by reading the code (which weights _score_player never references) and therefore could not see rookieRound1/rookieRound2, which ARE referenced by _score_player and so passed its test. They are inert for a different reason only live data reveals — the field they depend on does not exist in Sleeper's payload. Two of six weights remain dead after the remediation that the prior finding prompted.

whatWorks: The other four weights all fire and are correct: qbAnchor 16 times, skillStarter 25 (RB 9 / WR 8 / TE 8), skillCommittee 25 (RB 10 / WR 13 / TE 2), idpStarter 35 across DB/LB/DE/DL/DT/CB. _draft_round itself is defensively written and returns None cleanly rather than throwing; the defect is that its input never exists.
rootCause: The tier was designed against a field Sleeper's player endpoint does not publish, and nothing ever asserted the field's presence. tests/api/test_team_assignment.py pins the weight-key SET (that every declared weight is read by _score_player) but constructs its own fixture metas with draft_round injected, so it proves the code path exists while proving nothing about whether real data ever reaches it — the exact blind spot that let a dead tier ship as a live knob.
requiredRepair: Two acceptable repairs, and the module's own stated policy picks the second. (a) Source real draft capital: the rookie draft round is available from nflverse (the same release family src/bdvm/schedule.py already fetches) and the platform separately carries rookie draft-slot priors in scripts/bdvm_build_baseline.py — join on gsis_id, which IS on the Sleeper record. (b) Delete T4 and both weights outright, exactly as eliteProductionTop10/Top24 and idpElite were deleted on 2026-08-04 for being unread, and drop 'rookies with high draft capital' from the JSX explainer. Whichever is chosen, add a test that asserts against the REAL data/public_league/nfl_players.json vocabulary — a weight declared in config must be demonstrably reachable on live input, not just on a hand-built fixture.
dependencies: An external draft-capital feed if repair (a) is taken; none if (b).

title: The best-ball 'no fixed starting lineup' concern does not apply — starter/backup is read from Sleeper's NFL depth chart, not the fantasy lineup — but 35 of 666 rostered players carry no depth data and kickers are structurally unscorable in a league with a K slot
claimUnderTest: Prompt section 32 asks whether 'starters' and 'backups' are identified correctly in a BEST BALL league, where there is no fixed starting lineup.
observed: The concern is misplaced, and I could not reproduce it as a defect: _score_player never reads the fantasy lineup. 'Starter' means meta['depth_chart_order'] == 1 and 'committee' means depth_chart_order in (2,3) — Sleeper's NFL depth-chart position for that player on his NFL club. Best ball changes only how a fantasy lineup is set; it has no bearing on an NFL depth chart, and the feature's whole purpose is NFL-team correlation, so the NFL depth chart is the correct input. Confirmed in the live league: settings.best_ball == 1 and roster_positions carries a full explicit starting set (QB/2RB/3WR/2TE/2FLEX/SUPER_FLEX/K/3DL/3LB/3DB + 37 BN), and the scores reproduce exactly without any lineup input. Two real, smaller gaps do exist. (1) Coverage: 35 of 666 rostered players have depth_chart_order == null, so every skill and IDP tier silently skips them — they are indistinguishable in the output from players scored at zero. (2) Vocabulary: _SKILL_POSITIONS and _IDP_POSITIONS between them cover QB/RB/WR/TE/DL/DE/DT/LB/DB/CB/S, which leaves 20 rostered players permanently unscorable — 19 kickers and 1 'SS'. The kicker case is not hypothetical roster clog: roster_positions contains a K starting slot, so every one of the 12 teams is required to roster a kicker and no kicker can ever contribute a point toward his NFL team. 'S' is in the IDP set but Sleeper emits 'SS'/'FS', so the safety alias is the wrong string.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python -c "import json,collections;pl=json.load(open('data/public_league/nfl_players.json'));s=json.load(open('data/public_league/snapshot.json'));cur=[x for x in s['seasons'] if str(x['season'])=='2026'][0];print('best_ball',cur['league']['settings'].get('best_ball'));ap=[p for r in cur['rosters'] for p in (r.get('players') or [])];SK={'RB','WR','TE'};ID={'DL','DE','DT','LB','DB','CB','S'};print('rostered',len(ap));print('depth null',sum(1 for p in ap if (pl.get(str(p)) or {}).get('depth_chart_order') is None));print('unscorable pos',collections.Counter((pl.get(str(p)) or {}).get('position') for p in ap if (pl.get(str(p)) or {}).get('position') not in SK|ID|{'QB'}))"
reproduction.expected: if the best-ball concern were real, the scorer would have to consult starters/matchup lineups and would disagree with a depth-chart-only recomputation
reproduction.actual: best_ball 1; rostered 666; depth null 35; unscorable pos Counter({'K': 19, 'SS': 1}) — and the depth-chart-only recomputation in W28-F002 matches the live payload on all 12 managers with 0 mismatches

userImpact: A manager expanding 'Show breakdown' sees a player omitted with no explanation in two distinct cases that look identical: the player genuinely scored zero, or the model had no depth-chart data for him / has no rule for his position. A manager who rosters a starting kicker on, say, Baltimore gets zero Baltimore correlation from him even though the league forces him to roster a kicker. Low severity because the output is an entertainment/flavour mapping, not a trade or lineup decision.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers depth-chart sourcing or position-vocabulary coverage in this module (PRIOR-A03-F17, the only team_assignment prior, is about config knobs). Recorded partly as a verified NEGATIVE: the best-ball starter/backup suspicion raised in the prompt does not reproduce.

whatWorks: 631 of 666 rostered players (94.7%) carry depth_chart_order and are scored. The best-ball-independence of the model is a correct design choice, and the IDP gate (_league_idp_enabled reading roster_positions for DL/LB/DB slots) correctly returns True for this league, which is why 35 IDP contributions appear on the live payload.
rootCause: _IDP_POSITIONS was written against a guessed Sleeper position vocabulary ('S') rather than the observed one ('SS'/'FS'), and no tier was ever written for K. Missing depth_chart_order is treated as 'not a starter' rather than 'unknown', so absent data and a zero score are conflated.
requiredRepair: Add 'SS' and 'FS' to _IDP_POSITIONS (one-line, matches the existing pattern of listing raw Sleeper codes). Decide explicitly about K — either a kickerStarter weight or a code comment stating kickers are deliberately excluded, so the omission is a decision rather than an oversight. Optionally surface depth-unknown players in the contributors list at 0 points with reason 'no depth chart data', which is the same honest-omission posture the codebase already uses for assetsUnpricedByBoard in src/trade/finder.py and unpricedPickCount in the draft-capital fallback.

title: The 15-point qualification threshold leaves 5 of 12 managers with only their favorite team, so the 'up to 3 NFL teams' promise delivers a mean of 1.92 — and the config's own note flags this exact knob as untuned
claimUnderTest: The section header promises 'Each manager is mapped to 1-3 NFL teams ... Teams scoring at least 15 pts qualify; max 3 NFL teams per manager.' config/team_assignment.json's thresholds._doc states outright that removing the double-counted elite-production tier 'lowered every roster score' and that assignmentMinPoints 'is the knob to retune if too few NFL teams qualify' — i.e. the repo already suspects this number is stale and never measured it.
observed: Measured on the live payload: teams-per-manager distribution is {1: 5, 2: 3, 3: 4}, mean 1.92 against a cap of 3, and 5 of 12 managers (Collin, Jason, Roy, Ty, jstuedle) show only their favorite with no roster-based team at all. Their nearest misses are close to the line, not far from it — Collin's second-best NFL team is BUF at 14 (threshold 15), Jason's is WAS at 14, jstuedle's best team of any kind is TB at 12 while his own favorite KC scores only 6. Because the favorite bypasses the threshold, jstuedle's card displays 'Kansas City Chiefs FAVORITE' with the score suppressed entirely (the JSX prints 'N pts from roster' only when score > 0, so jstuedle's card reads 'FAVORITE · 6 pts from roster' while Brent's BUF at 0 renders as a bare 'FAVORITE' with no number at all). Separately, the output has no uniqueness constraint: 19 distinct NFL franchises are used across 12 managers, with HOU assigned to 4 different managers (Ty, Eric, Kitch and Joey all declare it as favorite) and KC to 2 (Joel's favorite and Brent's roster-based qualifier). That is defensible for a 'which NFL teams do you correlate with' readout but wrong for anything named 'assignment' that implies exclusivity, and nothing in the UI states which of the two it is.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python -c "import json,collections;a=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W28/team-assignment-live.json'))['data']['assignments'];n=[len(x['nflTeams']) for x in a];print('dist',dict(collections.Counter(n)),'mean',round(sum(n)/len(n),4));ab=collections.Counter(t['abbr'] for x in a for t in x['nflTeams']);print('distinct franchises',len(ab),'duplicated',{k:v for k,v in ab.items() if v>1})"
reproduction.expected: a distribution centred near the advertised cap of 3 if the threshold were tuned to the current post-T3-removal weights

userImpact: Five of twelve managers open the tab and see a single card entry that is just the favorite they declared by hand in a config file — the entire roster-correlation half of the feature produces nothing for them, and the explainer above it still promises 1-3 teams. Nobody trades or starts a player because of it, hence P3, but the feature reads as broken to 42% of the league.

priorFinding.note: New. PRIOR-A03-F17 explicitly notes that 'only assignmentMinPoints reaches the UI' and treats it as the one knob that works, but never measured what it produces. It is the removal of the weights that finding prompted which left the threshold mis-scaled.

whatWorks: The cap and the sort are both correct: roster_based is ordered by (-score, abbr) and sliced to remaining_capacity, the favorite always occupies slot 0 and always counts toward the cap, and no manager exceeds 3. The threshold is read from config at request time, so retuning it needs no redeploy exactly as the config claims.
rootCause: assignmentMinPoints 15 was set against the pre-2026-08-04 weight scale, where a primary QB scored 13 and a primary skill player 8. Removing the double-counting T3 tier dropped those to 10 and 5 — roughly a 38% cut to every roster score — but the threshold was left at 15. The config file documents the cause and explicitly defers the fix.
requiredRepair: Scale the threshold with the weights: 15 * (10/13) ~ 11.5, so 11 or 12 restores the pre-change qualification rate. Verify by re-running the reproduction command and checking the distribution, not by reasoning about it. Separately, either state in the JSX explainer that NFL teams are not exclusive across managers, or add a uniqueness pass if exclusivity is actually what 'assignment' is meant to mean — that is a product decision, not a bug fix.
dependencies: Interacts with W28-F003: repairing the dead rookie tier would itself raise scores and change the right threshold, so fix F003 first and tune the threshold once, afterwards.

title: The Team Assignment component's header comment states its data is cached for 30 minutes; the actual public-league snapshot TTL is 300 seconds
claimUnderTest: frontend/app/league/sections/team-assignment.jsx lines 13-16: 'Server-computed by src/api/team_assignment.py; re-runs whenever the contract is re-built (per-request, cached at the public-league snapshot layer for 30 min).'
observed: The public-league snapshot TTL is _PUBLIC_LEAGUE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = int(os.getenv('PUBLIC_LEAGUE_CACHE_TTL', '300')) — 5 minutes, not 30 — and the same constant sets the HTTP header 'public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300'. The live /api/public/league/metrics endpoint reports cacheTtlSeconds directly. A 6x overstatement of staleness in the one comment a developer reads before asking 'why is my roster change not showing up' points them at the wrong layer entirely.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && SECRET=$(cat /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/e2e_secret.txt) && curl -s -c /tmp/w28.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET" -o /dev/null && curl -s -b /tmp/w28.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/metrics | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('cacheTtlSeconds'))" && grep -n 'cached at the public-league snapshot layer' frontend/app/league/sections/team-assignment.jsx

userImpact: No user-visible wrong number. Developer-facing only: someone debugging apparent staleness in the Team Assignment tab will look for a 30-minute cache that does not exist and miss the two layers that do — the 300s snapshot SWR window and the generation-keyed response-bytes memo.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior index. Same class as PRIOR-A07-F11 (ops docs describing a topology that no longer exists), but a different file and a different subsystem.

whatWorks: The rest of the comment is accurate: the section IS server-computed per request by src/api/team_assignment.py and does re-run on every contract rebuild.
rootCause: Comment drift — the number was either never checked against server.py or was accurate against an older TTL default.
